title: The enriched coinduction comparison sends the identity class to its counit
statement: Let $f:S\to B$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings and let $U:D(B)\to D(S)$ be restriction on their ordinary unbounded module derived categories. Let $C:D(S)\to D(B)$ and $\epsilon:UC\to\operatorname{id}$ be the canonical derived coinduction and the counit of its actual restriction/coinduction adjunction [def-trf-derived-coinduction]. Let $\theta_{X,V}:U\operatorname{RHom}_B(X,CV)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{RHom}_S(UX,V)$ be the specific natural comparison selected from [lem-trf-algebraic-shriek-derived-hom-adjunction], with its prescribed localization formula on K-injective models. Let $\eta_f:S[0]\to U(B[0])$ be the map induced by $f$, using the native derived unit and single-functor comparisons. For a derived morphism $h:A\to D$, write $c_R(h):R[0]\to\operatorname{RHom}_R(A,D)$ for $\operatorname{curry}'(h)$ in the native closed structure [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. Then, for every $V\in D(S)$, the following maps from $S[0]$ to $\operatorname{RHom}_S(UCV,V)$ are equal: $\eta_f\,;\,U(c_B(\operatorname{id}_{CV}))\,;\,\theta_{CV,V}=c_S(\epsilon_V)$. No boundedness or flatness hypotheses are imposed.

proof.text: Choose an S-K-injective complex I representing V. By [lem-trf-algebraic-shriek-derived-hom-adjunction], J=coinductionComplexFunctor(f)(I) is B-K-injective. Transport C(V) and its identity to Q(J) and the identity chain map of J using the canonical derivedCoinductionModel. The same theorem identifies the chosen enriched comparison on these representatives with localization of its coordinate map T, sandwiched between the canonical Hom-model comparisons.

proof.text: The coordinate formula for T sends the degree-zero identity cocycle of Hom_B(J,J) to the cocycle x ↦ x(1) of Hom_S(UJ,I). The global class of a degree-zero cocycle is its map from the single free rank-one module. Restriction followed by the scalar map S→B preserves that class, because 1 maps to 1. The Hom-model comparisons are transposes of signed evaluation; on a degree-zero cocycle the sign is one. Hence the left side of the claimed equality is the curry-prime class of the localized evaluation-at-one chain map, transported by the canonical coinduction model. More explicitly, construct the class as mkHomFromSingle of r ↦ r·ofHom(id_J). The coordinate evaluation formula of [lem-pod-projective-hom-evaluation-model] gives ρ_J⁻¹ ; (J tensor class) ; ev = id_J because the Hom degree is zero. Uncurrying after Q, tensorator naturality and the lax monoidal right-unit law identify its localized class with curry-prime(id_QJ). The identical calculation over S applies to evaluation-at-one.

proof.text: The counit-model clause of [lem-trf-derived-coinduction-adjunction] identifies precisely this transported evaluation-at-one map with the counit of the actual derived restriction/coinduction adjunction. Naturality of the enriched comparison and the counit transports the resulting equality along the K-injective representation isomorphism back to V. This uses no flatness of B over S and no boundedness assumption.

theorem derived_coinduction_enriched_class (f : S →+* B) :
    ∀ V : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} S),
      coinductionScalarUnit f ≫ (restrictScalars f).mapDerivedCategory.map
          (MonoidalClosed.curry' (𝟙 ((derivedCoinduction f).obj V))) ≫
        (coinductionEnrichedHomIso f).hom.app (op ((derivedCoinduction f).obj V), V) =
      MonoidalClosed.curry' ((derivedCoinductionAdjunction f).counit.app V)
